name: Agent Setup Checklist
summary: Install an agent, connect MCP servers, add skills, and verify the setup.
description: Agent Setup Checklist is a practical onboarding workflow for moving from a fresh agent install to a verified working local toolchain. It is designed for users who do not yet know whether their problem is agent configuration, MCP startup, missing PATH, bad permissions, or unclear project instructions.
installSummary: This is a workflow checklist, not a command-line package. Copy it into the project's docs or agent instruction folder, then run through each verification step whenever a new agent or MCP server is added.

installSteps.title: Create a setup note in the repo
installSteps.body: Add a short setup document such as `docs/agent-setup.md` or a section in AGENTS.md. The point is to make local expectations explicit instead of relying on memory.

installSteps.title: List the supported agents
installSteps.body: Record which agents are officially supported for this project and which are experimental. This prevents users from applying Claude-specific instructions to Codex or Cursor without translation.

installSteps.title: Record MCP servers and skills
installSteps.body: For each MCP server or skill, include purpose, install path, secret requirements, verification prompt, and failure symptoms.

agentSetups.summary: Codex projects should keep setup notes close to the repo and make MCP config explicit.

steps.title: Project instructions
steps.body: Put repo-specific behavior in AGENTS.md or the configured project instruction file.

steps.title: MCP check
steps.body: After adding an MCP server, ask Codex to list available tools or perform a small action that requires that server.

agentSetups.summary: Claude Code users should separate persistent repo instructions from one-off review or build commands.

steps.title: CLAUDE.md
steps.body: Use CLAUDE.md for stable project rules, test commands, and safety constraints.

agentSetups.summary: Qwen Code setup should call out whether MCP settings are project-scoped or user-scoped.

steps.title: Scope check
steps.body: Record whether settings live in `.qwen/settings.json` or `~/.qwen/settings.json` so users know what changed.

primaryUseCases: Onboard a new machine or contributor into an agent-heavy project.
Debug why an MCP server appears installed but the agent cannot use it.
Create a repeatable acceptance checklist before recommending an agent setup publicly.
Document the difference between skills, MCP servers, CLI tools, and workflows for one project.
highlights: Keeps setup as a repeatable workflow instead of scattered chat history.
Separates install, configuration, verification, and troubleshooting.
Works for public directory entries and internal team docs.
Avoids fake one-command installs for workflows that are really editorial or operational templates.

configuration.title: Recommended checklist shape
configuration.body: Use the same headings for every supported tool so users can compare entries quickly.
configuration.code:
## Tool name
Purpose:
Supported agents:
Install:
Config:
Secrets:
Verification prompt:
Failure symptoms:
Rollback:

verificationSteps.title: Run a smoke prompt
verificationSteps.body: For each agent, run one prompt that requires a configured MCP server and one prompt that requires a project instruction.

verificationSteps.title: Record failure mode
verificationSteps.body: If setup fails, document the exact symptom: missing command, auth failure, permission denial, timeout, no tool call, or wrong project scope.

troubleshooting.title: Everything looks installed but the agent does not use it
troubleshooting.body: Add an explicit project rule telling the agent when to call the tool, then test with a prompt that cannot be answered well without it.

troubleshooting.title: Works in terminal but not in GUI agent
troubleshooting.body: Check PATH and environment variables. GUI apps often do not inherit the same shell setup.

securityNotes: Do not commit API keys in setup docs.
Record which tools can access browsers, files, terminals, or authenticated services.
Add rollback steps for MCP servers that modify global user config.
limitations: A checklist does not install tools by itself.
Agent-specific commands still need to be verified against current vendor docs.
The workflow is only useful if the team actually updates it after setup changes.
maintenanceNotes: Review the checklist whenever a new agent, MCP server, or skill is added.
Keep tool entries short enough to scan but complete enough to reproduce.
